summary.intent: Execute Phase 26 (Observability & UX Tuning) of the cipher-box project, which involved creating Grafana alert rules and tuning client timeout/retry constants. Also fix a Grafana free tier series cardinality limit being hit.
summary.outcome: Phase 26 executed successfully with 2/2 plans complete and 14/14 must-haves verified. Additionally diagnosed and fixed Grafana series cardinality exhaustion via Alloy metric filtering and HTTP route label normalization. PR #366 created; a CI test failure from the timeout value change was caught and fixed.

repo: The GSD workflow system requires plans to exist before execute-phase can run — plan-phase must be run first if the phase directory is empty.
The project uses Grafana Alloy (River config at `docker/alloy-config.river`) to scrape and remote-write metrics. Kubo and Someguy are scraped alongside the CipherBox API.

The dashboard only uses 6 Kubo/Someguy metrics: `go_goroutines`, `go_memstats_alloc_bytes`, `libp2p_swarm_connections_opened_total`, `libp2p_swarm_connections_closed_total`, `libp2p_network_in_bytes_total`, `libp2p_network_out_bytes_total`.
Alert rules (Phase 26-01) only reference `cipherbox_*` metrics — no external metric dependency in alerting.
NestJS route templates already parameterize known routes (`:id`, `:cid`); the gap was unmatched bot/scanner paths creating unbounded cardinality.
The `delegated-routing.client.spec.ts` had hardcoded timeout values (1000ms, 2000ms) that needed updating when `baseDelayMs` was changed from 1000→500ms.

code.finding: Unmatched routes (bot scanners, 404s) were creating unique label values per path, exploding HTTP histogram cardinality. Fixed by collapsing unmatched routes to `/:unmatched`. The `normalizeRoute` method was removed entirely — matched routes use NestJS parameterized templates.

Added a `prometheus.relabel` stage to filter Kubo and Someguy scrapes to only the 6 metrics actually used in dashboards. Previously all metrics from these high-cardinality Go/libp2p services were forwarded.
Three assertions hardcoded old baseDelayMs values: expected 1000ms (now 500ms) and 2000ms (now 1000ms for second backoff). These broke CI and needed updating after the timeout tuning in Phase 26-02.
Timeout comments referenced ephemeral benchmark data ('~44x client-side pin p99 of 227ms'). Cleaned up to describe intent only.

Two separate `sed` calls combined into one with `-e` flags; delimiter changed from `/` to `|` to avoid breakage if UIDs contain `/`. Also scoped `--dry-run` flag parsing to `${@:4}` to avoid collision with positional params.

workflow: When `git diff main..HEAD` shows 'removals' of features that were never added on the branch, it means main moved ahead after branching — the diff shows the inverse of what main gained, not what the branch removed.

Merging main into a long-lived feature branch can cause planning doc conflicts (ROADMAP.md, STATE.md) that require manual resolution to preserve both the new phase's progress and prior phases' completion marks.
The GSD tools run against the current working directory — if invoked from the wrong repo/worktree, init will return incorrect state (missing plans, wrong phase data).
Grafana Cloud Free tier has a 10,000 active series limit. Kubo (libp2p/DHT metrics) alone can exceed this; filtering at the Alloy relay layer before remote_write is the right mitigation point.
CI test failures from changed constant values (timeouts, delays) are easily missed during code review if tests use hardcoded expected values rather than referencing the same constants.

friction: execute-phase was invoked before plan-phase had been run, producing a confusing 'no plans found' error on a phase that had research and context committed.
GSD init tools ran against the wrong working directory initially, causing incorrect phase state to be reported (missing plans that actually existed).
Merging main required manual conflict resolution of multiple planning docs (ROADMAP.md) to restore Phase 24 and 25 completion marks that were clobbered by the merge strategy.
CI caught a test regression (hardcoded timeout values in `delegated-routing.client.spec.ts`) that should have been caught locally before push.
Investigation of PR #365 review comment was interrupted mid-execution when the target branch was in a different git worktree.
open_items: PR #365 (`fix/recovery-e2e-kubo-ipns`) has an outstanding nitpick review comment that was not applied — interrupted before the fix was made.
Grafana alert JSON (~877 lines across 5 files) has significant structural duplication that could be reduced to a config table + template — deferred as a larger restructuring.
The 5s delegated routing timeout may be aggressive under load against `delegated-ipfs.dev` (external DHT-backed service) — flagged to monitor post-deploy.
The `ipHash: ''` empty string failing strict 64-char hex validation was flagged as a bug in pre-existing code (not Phase 26) — not addressed.

Unrelated changes on the branch (desktop updater removal, device registry v2→v1 downgrade, bin auto-repair removal, load test/recovery E2E deletions) from `carry forward: uncommitted session files` commits were identified but not investigated or resolved.
